Tovste Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Tovste holds one of the most significant sites in this entire collection: the grave of Sarah, mother of the Baal Shem Tov, founder of Hasidism, who himself resided in the town from 1730 to 1740, a period during which a Beit Midrash, bathhouse, and mikvah all operated locally. By the late 19th century, the Chortkiv, Vizhnitz, and Kopichinitz Hasidic dynasties — the first two documented at their own founding towns elsewhere in this collection — all had followers in Tovste, and the Jewish population peaked at 2,157 (67.4 percent of the town) in 1880. Between late August and early October 1942, 1,200 Jews were deported to the Bełżec death camp, with 120 more murdered on the spot; a ghetto operated from December 1942 until its liquidation in June 1943. A monument was erected at this cemetery after the war.
